docRequirement: admin-setup.md:54 — "A configured [`policyHelper`](/docs/en/settings#compute-managed-settings-with-a-policy-helper) preempts all four sources: its output becomes the only managed configuration for the run." settings.md:304 defines the key as an "Admin-deployed executable that computes managed settings dynamically at startup. Only honored from MDM or a system `managed-settings.json` file", and settings.md:633-:645 fixes its shape and semantics: the object accepts `path` (absolute path to the executable), `timeoutMs` and `refreshIntervalMs` (`0` disables refresh, otherwise at least `60000`); the helper writes a JSON envelope to stdout whose settings sit under a `managedSettings` key ("a bare settings object parses with `managedSettings` undefined and applies nothing"), optionally alongside `claudeMd` and `appendSystemPrompt`; that object "becomes the only managed settings source for the run, taking precedence over remote, MDM, and file-based sources"; and "When the helper exits non-zero at startup, Claude Code prints the error and refuses to start." settings.md:670 adds that while a helper is configured its output is also the only source the cross-source lock keys are read from, and settings.md:633 requires `policyHelper` to be IGNORED from every non-admin scope, server-managed settings included.
current: Nessy has exactly two managed sources and no helper tier. `EnforcedManagedPolicySeams` declares only `file` and `delivered` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:53-58) and `resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy` composes exactly those two (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:127-139). `ManagedPolicyWinnerV1` is `'delivered' | 'file' | 'none'` (packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:130) and `composeManagedPolicySources` has no third branch (packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:184-213). The file loader reads JSON and nothing else: `loadManagedPiPolicyWithDiagnostics` reads `managed-policy.json` plus `managed-policy.d/*.json` through `readHostOwnedJson`, merges them and hands the merged object to `parseManagedPiPolicyTolerantV1` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:327-377); there is no spawn anywhere on the path. `policyHelper` is not a schema key — `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` is 34 entries and does not contain it (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534) — so `refuseUnknownKeys` strips it and records the drop `invalid managed Pi policy key: policyHelper` with disposition `stripped` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:727-733). That drop is printed at boot by `reportManagedPolicyDrops` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:247) and listed by the doctor report (apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:80). The identifier survives in tracked source at exactly one place, a docblock quoting Claude's own precedence chain: packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:29 — " * rather than merged\", `policyHelper` > remote > MDM > file-based > HKCU." Nessy also ships no MDM/plist/registry managed source at all (binary-safe grep for `plist`, `com.anthropic.claudecode`, `HKLM`, `SOFTWARE\\Policies` across packages/shared/src, packages/server-core/src, apps/electron/src, apps/cli/src returns only an unrelated dock-icon comment), so the system file `managedPiPolicyPathForPlatform` resolves — `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json`, `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json`, `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-52) — is the only scope in which a helper could ever be configured here. No helper-executable mechanism exists elsewhere to have been misnamed: the only sibling, MCP `headersHelper`, is explicitly read-and-reported-not-implemented in a different subsystem (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1047-1055, packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:137-147).
divergence: This is an absent mechanism, not a key-name or value mismatch — nothing about `policyHelper` is right except that it is refused loudly instead of silently. Four specified behaviours have no implementation: (1) no parse of the `{path, timeoutMs, refreshIntervalMs}` object, (2) no execution of the named executable and no read of its stdout `managedSettings` envelope, (3) no third, highest tier in the managed precedence chain — `composeManagedPolicySources` cannot express "preempts all four sources" because its winner union has no `'helper'` member, and (4) no non-zero-exit startup refusal; `createStorageRuntime` has no failure mode for managed-policy resolution at all (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:234-258). One documented behaviour we already get for free and must keep: settings.md:633's "Claude Code ignores `policyHelper` … including … server-managed settings" is satisfied today by `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` omitting the key, so the delivered/wire path strips it. Two envelope fields have no counterpart in our schema and would be dropped even after the helper runs: `claudeMd` and `appendSystemPrompt` — `claudeRules` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:420-424) is `allow`/`ask`/`deny` rule strings, not markdown context or a system-prompt suffix.

change.what: Add `export interface ManagedPolicyHelperV1 { readonly path: string; readonly timeoutMs?: number; readonly refreshIntervalMs?: number }` and `export function parseManagedPolicyHelperV1(value: unknown, sink: ManagedDropSink): ManagedPolicyHelperV1 | undefined`. Validate per settings.md:637-:641: `path` must be a non-empty ABSOLUTE path (reject relative, reject any C0/C1 control char, cap length like the other string fields); `timeoutMs` a positive finite number with a default the implementer records; `refreshIntervalMs` either exactly `0` (refresh disabled) or `>= 60000` — anything between is a defect, drop it and disable refresh rather than guessing an interval. Any defect in `path` drops the whole helper (`stripped`) so the run falls back to the ordinary two-source composition. Do NOT add `policyHelper` to MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS at :501-534: doing so would make it deliverable over the gateway payload, which settings.md:633 forbids, and would put it in `isManagedPolicyTightening`'s loop at :629. Leave `refuseUnknownKeys` at :727-733 exactly as it is — the loader removes the key before the parse (see the loader entry), so the wire path keeps stripping it and the file path stops seeing it.

New module. `runManagedPolicyHelper(helper: ManagedPolicyHelperV1, deps): ManagedPiPolicyParseV1` — (a) validate the executable with the SAME host-ownership regime the loader already applies to policy files: `lstat` must be a non-symlink regular file, `realpathSync(path) === path`, and `assertPosixOwnerAndMode` (uid 0, no group/other write) — reuse or export the existing helpers at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:74-86 rather than writing a second copy; (b) `spawnSync(helper.path, [], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: helper.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT, maxBuffer: MAX_MANAGED_POLICY_BYTES, env: <a minimal, explicitly-listed env>, shell: false })`; (c) non-zero exit, spawn error, or timeout throws an error carrying a sanitized, length-bounded stderr excerpt (settings.md:645's "prints the error and refuses to start"); (d) `JSON.parse` stdout, take `envelope.managedSettings` only — a bare settings object at the top level must apply NOTHING, per settings.md:643, which is a required negative test; (e) run that object through `parseManagedPiPolicyTolerantV1` with `source` set to the helper path so drops attribute correctly. Never log stdout: it can carry an `env` block with a credential, the same reason packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts:144-157 writes its cache at 0600.

After `mergeManagedPolicySources` at :370 and BEFORE `parseManagedPiPolicyTolerantV1` at :371, extract and delete `policyHelper` from the merged record. If present, `parseManagedPolicyHelperV1` it; if it parses, call `runManagedPolicyHelper` and return ITS parse result instead of the file's, marking the load. Widen `ManagedPiPolicyLoadV1` with `readonly source?: 'file' | 'helper'` (or a `helper?: { path: string }` field the doctor can print) — the winner label downstream needs to know. Add a `runHelper` seam to `ManagedPiPolicyLoaderDependencies` so tests never spawn. Decide and RECORD one thing the doc does not address: whether a `policyHelper` in a `managed-policy.d/` fragment is honoured under the existing merge order or dropped with a reason. The base file alone is the conservative reading of settings.md:304's "a system `managed-settings.json` file`"; whichever is chosen, the reason belongs in the constant's comment, per this repo's practice at :54-61.

change.what: Add `'helper'` to the winner union at :130. Add `readonly helper?: ManagedPiPolicyV1 | undefined` to `ManagedPolicySourcesV1`. In `composeManagedPolicySources`, short-circuit FIRST: when `helper !== undefined`, return `Object.freeze({ policy: helper, winner: 'helper' })` with no `composeNetworkLock` and no `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` union — settings.md:670 says that while a helper is configured "its output is the only source these checks read", so the cross-source carve-out at :163-174/:201-205 must be SKIPPED, not applied. Gate on the helper being configured, not on `carriesManagedSettings(helper)`: settings.md:643 makes an empty `managedSettings` apply nothing, and that is still the helper winning the tier. Extend the § "The cross-source exception" block at :37-60 with the helper carve-out, and update :29's chain quote to say we now implement the first hop.

Carry the loader's helper marker through. Simplest shape that keeps one definition: `resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy` reads `file.source === 'helper'` and passes `{ helper: file.policy }` instead of `{ file: file.policy }` into the composition; `fileCarriesSettings` must then be computed from the FILE policy the helper preempted, not the helper's output, or the shadow warning below reports the wrong thing. Add a `helperPath` (or reuse the load marker) to `EnforcedManagedPolicyV1` so the doctor can name it. In the catch branch at :299-330, a helper that threw must NOT silently degrade to the delivered/file composition — that is exactly the failure settings.md:645 says must stop the run; keep the thrown reason in the drop list and let the caller decide.

`WINNER_LABEL` is `Readonly<Record<ManagedPolicyWinnerV1, string>>`, so widening the union breaks this at compile time — add `helper: 'Managed settings (policy helper)'`. In `buildConfigDoctorReport` add the `helper` branch printing the sanitized helper path beside the label, mirroring the `delivered`/`file` branches at :427-432. Extend `shadowedManagedFileWarning` (or add a sibling) to fire for `winner === 'helper'` with `fileCarriesSettings === true`: the helper preempting a deployed, valid policy file is the same invisible state the function exists for, one tier up, and leaving it at `winner !== 'delivered'` silently reintroduces it.

`resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy()` at :234 currently cannot fail. Give it a failure mode for the helper's non-zero exit and decide the product answer explicitly: settings.md:645 binds Claude Code to print the error and refuse to start, which is straightforward for the headless server (`packages/server`) and is a real product decision for the desktop shell (a blocking startup dialog vs. refusing to launch). Whatever is chosen, record it as a categorised deviation — a silent fall-through to the file/delivered composition is the one option the doc excludes, because it turns a broken fleet helper into an unpoliced client. Note the coupling at :241: the composed policy feeds `setManagedModelPolicy`, so a helper that returns an over-narrow `availableModels` empties a user's model list.

`refreshIntervalMs` needs no new adoption machinery — reuse this. Schedule a timer at `helper.refreshIntervalMs` (skip when `0`) that re-runs the helper through the existing `resolveManagedPiPolicy` seam wired at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:455; `refreshManagedPiPolicy` already holds a non-tightening change to a turn boundary via `isManagedPolicyTightening`. Do not add a second adoption path that bypasses that gate.

Helper present wins over both `delivered` and `file`; helper with an EMPTY policy still wins and enforces nothing (settings.md:643); the cross-source lock keys are NOT unioned when a helper is configured, even when the file sets `sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly` (settings.md:670) — that negative is the one a naive implementation gets wrong.

Helper extracted from the merged document and no longer reported as an invalid key; a helper whose executable is not root-owned / is a symlink is refused; non-zero exit propagates the fatal error with stderr sanitized; a stdout envelope WITHOUT `managedSettings` applies nothing; timeout is enforced. Drive it all through the new `runHelper` seam so no test spawns a process.

Pin the behaviour we already have and must keep: a `policyHelper` key inside a DELIVERED payload is still stripped with `invalid managed Pi policy key: policyHelper` (settings.md:633 ignores it from server-managed settings). Without this pin, adding the key to the schema later silently opens a remote-code-execution path over the gateway.

The recorded reason — "`policyHelper` and `wslInheritsWindowsSettings` (`:129` — OS-policy sources only)" — is half-covering: it justifies excluding the helper from the server-DELIVERED channel and does not address the system FILE loader, which settings.md:304 names as a valid scope and which this fork ships. Rewrite it to say which half is out of scope, and update the R25b row at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:193 (currently "Record as C", i.e. still open) with whichever decision lands.

blastRadius: `ManagedPolicyWinnerV1` (packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:130) is read at packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts:43,65,231,254 and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:25,73; the exhaustive `Record<ManagedPolicyWinnerV1, string>` at config-doctor.ts:231 makes widening the union a compile error, which is the desired tripwire. `resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy` has 8 call sites: packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:234 and :455, packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:167 and :281, apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:80, plus packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/config-doctor-input.test.ts and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-delivered-policy.test.ts. The seam at storage-runtime.ts:455 (`resolveManagedPiPolicy`) feeds SessionManager's live re-read at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:3477-3500, covered by packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/managed-policy-reread.test.ts. storage-runtime.ts:241 pushes the composed policy into `setManagedModelPolicy`, so helper output reaches the model allowlist — the surface the inert-worklist warns permanently destroys a user's model list when mishandled. `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` has 6 readers in packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts and is pinned by packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/managed-policy-reread.test.ts, packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-delivered-policy.test.ts and packages/shared/src/marketplace/__tests__/delivered-marketplace-policy.test.ts — the plan above deliberately does not touch it, which keeps all four green. RISK TRIGGERS, both named explicitly: (1) this introduces a NEW PROCESS-SPAWN / ISOLATION boundary — a root-owned executable run at boot with the host's environment; without the uid-0/no-group-write/no-symlink regime already applied to policy files at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:74-86 and :229-264, the managed tier becomes a privilege-escalation path from a user-writable location. (2) it changes an ADMIN POLICY / permission-decision boundary, since the helper's output replaces the entire managed tier including `permissionDsl`, `claudeRules`, the plugin and MCP lists and the sandbox block. It does NOT cross a wire or persistence boundary: `ManagedPolicyWinnerV1` and `ManagedPiPolicyLoadV1` stay inside server-core/CLI/doctor rendering and never enter an RPC envelope, and no new file is written — provided the implementer does not cache helper output, for which the doc gives no contract. The gateway-delivered payload path (packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts) must remain unable to carry `policyHelper`.
userImpact: An administrator who deploys `{"policyHelper": {"path": "/usr/local/bin/nessy-policy"}}` in `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json` (or `/etc/nessy/`, or `%ProgramData%\Nessy\`) gets no policy computed and no executable run. The key is stripped by `refuseUnknownKeys` and the drop `invalid managed Pi policy key: policyHelper` prints at every startup via `reportManagedPolicyDrops` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:247) and appears in the `Managed settings` section of `nessy-general-agent doctor` (apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:80). So the failure is visible rather than silent — but the capability is entirely unavailable: fleet policy that has to be derived from device posture, user identity, or a remote lookup cannot be expressed at all, and the admin's only options are a static JSON file or the gateway-delivered payload. Because Nessy ships no MDM/plist/registry source either, the system file is the only place a helper could ever have been configured. Zero end-user surface — a developer using the app sees nothing.
